title: Journeys: A. J. W. (Anth Ginn)
author: Anth Ginn (handle AJW)
tradition: Divine Light Mission / Elan Vital (Prem Rawat, 'Knowledge'); former member of 25 years
locator_hints: Section on the friend's promise: 'you'll see this light, brighter than a thousand suns, better than acid'
Initiation, March 1973, section beginning 'Being ready meant understanding...': 'I didn't see light brighter than a thousand suns'
Section 'Premies should no longer practise...': late-1980s restriction of the first technique to formal sitting
'Forum Frolicks' / 'Wasting Time': lack of experience blamed on the practitioner
summary: A long memoir by a man who received the Knowledge in March 1973 and stayed twenty-five years. He had been told that in meditation he would see a light brighter than a thousand suns. Shown the four techniques, he saw no such light and heard no music, only a vague buzzing; the instructors' concern was whether he was 'ready', meaning convinced there was one Master and one method. He lived in ashrams with meditation every morning from six. He notes that in the late 1980s premies were told to stop practising the first technique through the day and to do it only when sitting, and that a meditator who did not experience 'infinite glory' was told the fault was his own impurity. He reports no later onset of light.
why_relevant: Long-term practitioner who was promised light, was taught the induction technique, and reports not seeing it across 25 years; documents how the organisation explained non-seeing.
